blockDescriptions.block_01: OS Foundations & System Structure — OS services, structures, kernel vs user mode
blockDescriptions.block_02: Processes & Inter-Process Communication — process lifecycle, shared memory, message passing
blockDescriptions.block_03: Threads & CPU Scheduling — threading models, scheduling criteria and algorithms
blockDescriptions.block_04: Process Synchronization — critical section, mutex/semaphores/monitors, classic sync problems
blockDescriptions.block_06: Memory Management — contiguous allocation, paging, virtual memory, page replacement
blockDescriptions.block_07: I/O Systems & File Storage — I/O interfaces, subsystem performance, file system implementation

requiredCourseModel.tierQuestionFocus: Prior exposure to systems/C programming and OS concepts before this course

personalizationRules: This is a REQUIRED, cumulative course — every enrolled student is examined on the entire syllabus. Every block MUST appear in every pathway. NEVER omit a block, and never drop a block's node count to zero, regardless of the student's background.

Every node MUST include syllabusBlockId set to exactly one block id from the catalog, and MUST include nodeRole (one of: core_required, scaffolding_catchup, enrichment_advanced, assessment) and a one-sentence personalizationRationale.

Personalization here means a FIXED DESTINATION with a PERSONALIZED ROUTE: the goal is to help a student with less prior exposure to systems/C programming catch up to their classmates FASTER, not to teach them less or teach them longer overall.

If the student reports little or no prior exposure to systems programming, C, or OS concepts (no_prior_exposure tier): add extra nodes tagged scaffolding_catchup concentrated in block_01 (OS Foundations) and block_02 (Processes & IPC), the two blocks that everything else depends on.

If the student reports some prior exposure (some_prior_exposure tier): include a moderate number of scaffolding_catchup nodes in block_01/block_02 — fewer than the no-prior-exposure case, more than the strong-exposure case.

If the student reports strong prior exposure (strong_prior_exposure tier, e.g. has already written multi-threaded C or systems code): keep block_01/block_02 to their floor-level core_required nodes only, and instead add enrichment_advanced nodes (harder edge cases, performance/design-tradeoff framing, connections to later blocks) — reinvest the freed-up capacity, do not shorten the pathway.

The TOTAL number of nodes must stay within the target node band (see requiredCourseModel.targetNodeBand) for every profile regardless of tier. Personalization must show up as a shift in the MIX of scaffolding_catchup vs. enrichment_advanced nodes, not as a longer or shorter pathway.

Every node's wording (description) may reflect the student's stated interests or goals (e.g., framing memory management with a database-systems analogy vs. a low-level hardware analogy), but this must NEVER change which blocks appear, how many nodes per block, or the presence of required content.
Every pathway must include at least one assessment-type node tied to the midterm-review material (in or after block_03) and one tied to the cumulative final-review material (in block_07).
